title: Royal Canadian Navy recruitment 2026 guide
metaDescription: Royal Canadian Navy recruitment 2026: who can join, age 17 to 57, citizenship or permanent residence, Grade 10 minimum, aptitude test and basic training.
headline: How to join the Royal Canadian Navy in 2026

sections.title: Who can join the Royal Canadian Navy
sections.content:
To join the Royal Canadian Navy you must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, be at least 17 years old, and have completed at least Grade 10 or Secondary IV in Quebec. Applicants under 18 need parental consent, and everyone must meet the Canadian Armed Forces common medical standard.

The upper age limit is 57 in general recruiting material, because members must be able to complete training and an initial term before the mandatory retirement age of 60. Officers normally need a university degree, while many sailor trades accept Grade 10 plus trade-specific maths or college training.

sections.title: Aptitude test, medical and training
sections.content:
Every applicant takes the Canadian Forces Aptitude Test, which assesses problem-solving, verbal and spatial ability, plus a medical exam, an interview and reliability screening. Your results help match you to trades such as marine technician, naval warfare officer, sonar operator or naval electronic sensor operator.

Basic training is the Basic Military Qualification course at the Canadian Forces Leadership and Recruit School in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec, followed by naval environmental training on either coast, in Halifax, Nova Scotia, or Esquimalt, British Columbia. Marine technicians then train for about 14 weeks at a naval fleet school.

sections.title: Naval Experience Program and careers
sections.content:
The Naval Experience Program is a one-year, continuous-intake trial that lets citizens and permanent residents experience navy life with no long-term strings attached. It includes basic training and naval training, then hands-on time at sea, after which participants can leave or continue into a regular career.

Longer careers offer job security, paid education in some trades, travel and progression from sailor to senior leadership. Because recruiting needs vary by trade, speaking to a recruiter early helps you target trades with open positions and funded education options.

faqs.q: How old do you have to be to join the Royal Canadian Navy?
faqs.a: You must be at least 17 years old to join, with parental consent if you are under 18, and recruiting material generally lists 57 as the upper age. The practical limit is the ability to finish training and a first term before the mandatory retirement age of 60, so older applicants should confirm their eligibility with a recruiter before applying.

faqs.q: Do you need to be a Canadian citizen to join the navy?
faqs.a: No, since late 2022 the Canadian Armed Forces have also accepted permanent residents, not only citizens. You must hold Canadian citizenship or permanent resident status under immigration law, meet the medical standard and pass the aptitude test, interview and reliability screening. Applicants without either status must gain permanent residence first.

faqs.q: What is the Naval Experience Program?
faqs.a: The Naval Experience Program is a one-year trial that lets Canadian citizens and permanent residents try navy life full-time or part-time, starting with basic training and naval environmental training in Halifax or Esquimalt. After the year you can leave with no further obligation or continue into a regular naval career, which makes it a low-risk way to test the service.
